newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell sharply to 961 million yuan from 3.332 billion yuan with the 60-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said trading was very dull with both banks and non-banking financial institutions reluctant to trade before July 1 which is a public holiday in China due to the takeover of Hong Kong.
Officials said the exchange had yet to decide a holiday schedule but nearly all other China's financial markets would close from Saturday to Tuesday to mark the event.
"Most financial institutions are unwilling to hold heavy positions before the expected long holiday," one trader said.
But traders said they believed turnover would rise to some extent on Thursday and Friday because Friday is the settlement date for the second quarter for all financial institutions.

Non-banking financial institutions including securities houses, who trade through the short-term financial centres, money borkerages run by the central bank, were comparatively active traders on Wednesday, traders said.
Traders said they expected the interbank rates to move narrrowly in the short term.
